newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM vows end prostitution, AIDS victims react.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM vows end prostitution, AIDS victims react.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Tuesday vowed to end rampant prostitution in northern provinces, sparking a heated response from AIDS workers and former prostitutes.

Chavalit told about 2,000 people who greeted him and other cabinet members who went to this northern town for a cabinet meeting that the government wanted first-hand information on how to end prostitution in the region.
Northern Thailand accounts for about half of the country's 800,000 cases of HIV, the virus that causes AIDS.

Non-governmental organisations say most of the country's prostitutes come from provinces in the north and a large number of them who have travelled to cities like Bangkok to work return to their villages once they get infected. They in turn, infect others.
AIDS is mostly transmitted in Thailand through heterosexual contact. Men often get the disease from a prostitute then infect their wives who in turn pass it on to unborn children, AIDS workers said.
Chavalit's remarks prompted retorts from prostitutes who became infected with HIV.

"We got the HIV virus from our work. We did it because we are poor, so the government can never resolve the problem of prostitution as long as people are still poor and uneducated," a member of the Friends of AIDS group said to another crowd of people who rallied separately from Chavalit's well-wishers to protest against the government.
Friends of AIDS estimates about 400,000 northerners between 20 and 40 are infected with HIV and about 20,000 of them are suffering from full-blown AIDS.
Anti-AIDS activists in Chiang Rai estimate about 12 people die each day in the north from AIDS.
Fat Kamhae, a 30-year old infected with AIDS, said his wife Tim died two years ago and he did not expect to survive past this year. He said people from his village die every day.
"In Thung Ang village of Chiengkhong district where about 2,000 people live, the elders go to funerals of young people every day," Fat said from his hospital bed.
But official records at the provincial health office show only three people die each day from the disease.

Friends of AIDS estimates that at least 60,000 children in northern Thailand are infected with HIV while the Chiang Rai health office estimates about six percent of pregnant women in the region have AIDS.
The World Health Organisation said earlier this month Thailand has the fourth largest number of AIDS cases in the world with nearly 60,000.
But this is only the number of officially-reported cases and health workers say the actual number is several times higher.
